answer: To join, an agent also submits a lotus challenge solved only through sustained compute. Agents must burn an umber-marked bond proving stake before voting, and each identity carries a lantern signature tied to a unique hardware root. Duplicating identities then costs real stake plus repeated proof-of-work, so sock-puppet swarms become economically unviable while honest agents recover their bonds after good behavior. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
